---
title: "Simulating SBML models"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This article takes a model from an SBML file to a simulation: reading it,
looking at what it holds, deriving its equations, and running them with
deSolve, events included. It ends with how the package is checked against
the SBML Test Suite.

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(zusbml)
```

## Reading a model

`sbml_read()` accepts a file path, a `file://` or `http(s)://` URL, the XML
as a string, or a raw vector. It reads SBML Level 3 Versions 1 and 2, and
Level 2 Versions 4 and 5, which it maps to their Level 3 meaning.

```{r}
m <- sbml_read(system.file("extdata", "dosing.xml", package = "zusbml"))
m
```

Every element kind is a data frame, with the SBML attributes as columns in
snake_case. Attributes a document leaves out are `NA`: Level 3 has no
defaults for them.

```{r}
sbml_parameters(m)[, c("id", "value", "constant")]
sbml_compartments(m)[, c("id", "size", "constant")]
```

Math is held as R expressions. `sbml_math()` shows it as R code.

```{r}
sbml_math(sbml_reactions(m)$kinetic_law)
```

A document that uses an SBML Level 3 package is refused by name, with a
`zusbml_unsupported` error; `ignore_packages = TRUE` reads its core model.
`sbml_check()` reports structural problems as a data frame and never
raises:

```{r}
sbml_check(m)
```

## Deriving the equations

`sbml_odes()` follows the Level 3 Version 2 specification to turn reactions
and rules into states and right-hand sides:

* a species whose symbol is an amount changes by stoichiometry times rate;
  one whose symbol is a concentration changes by that divided by its
  compartment's size;
* a reaction id stands for its rate, and is evaluated as an assignment;
* function definitions and local parameters are inlined.

```{r}
eq <- sbml_odes(m)
eq$states
eq$rhs
eq$assignments
eq$constants
sbml_initial_state(m)
```

Events are carried as data:

```{r}
str(eq$events[[1]][c("id", "trigger", "assignments")])
```

## Simulating

`sbml_derivs()` returns the derivative function deSolve calls, with what
else it needs as attributes: `y0`, the states at time 0 after any events
that fire then; `parms`; and, for a model with events, `rootfunc` and
`events`. Use `lsodar`, the deSolve method that finds roots.

```{r}
f <- sbml_derivs(m, outputs = "absorption")
out <- deSolve::ode(
  y = attr(f, "y0"),
  times = seq(0, 24, by = 0.25),
  func = f,
  parms = attr(f, "parms"),
  method = "lsodar",
  rootfunc = attr(f, "rootfunc"),
  events = attr(f, "events")
)
```

```{r, fig.alt = "Concentration of the drug in the central compartment over 24 hours: it rises to a peak near hour 2, falls, and after the second dose at hour 12 peaks again near hour 14."}
plot(out[, "time"], out[, "drug"], type = "l",
     xlab = "Time (hours)", ylab = "Concentration in central")
```

The event engine applies the SBML rules for events: a trigger fires when it
changes from false to true; `initialValue` says what it was before time 0;
a delay postpones execution, and a non-persistent event is canceled if its
trigger turns false meanwhile; events due at the same time run in priority
order, in random order when tied, so set a seed for a reproducible run.

## Writing

`sbml_write()` writes SBML Level 3 Version 2, whatever level the model was
read from, and reading the result back gives the same object:

```{r}
identical(sbml_read(sbml_write(m)), m)
```

`sbml_to_rxode2()` writes the equations as rxode2 model text. rxode2 cannot
express SBML events, so `events = "drop"` is needed for this model:

```{r}
cat(sbml_to_rxode2(m, events = "drop"))
```

## How it is checked

The package is tested against the
[SBML Test Suite](https://github.com/sbmlteam/sbml-test-suite) 3.5.0. Each
of its 1,692 Level 3 Version 2 semantic cases is read, written and read
back, derived, simulated with deSolve, and compared with the case's results
under its own absolute and relative tolerances. The 1,384 cases within the
supported set all pass; the 308 that need algebraic rules, the `delay`
csymbol, fast reactions or SBML packages are asserted to be refused. The
1,028 supported cases that also have a Level 2 Version 5 file pass from that
file too. Fifty curated BioModels are read, round-tripped and derived in CI.
Neither the suite nor the models are shipped: the suite is LGPL, and both
are downloaded by scripts in the repository's `tools/` directory.
